recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This portrait shows NGC 1515, a galaxy that astronomers classify as an intermediate barred spiral. It lies about 55 million light-years away in the constellation Dorado. The Dark Energy Camera captured it from the Blanco 4-meter Telescope, part of Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, which is a Program of NSF NOIRLab.

Spiral galaxies are flattened discs of stars, gas and dust whose arms wind out from a bright center. In a barred spiral, a straight band of stars runs across the middle, and the arms tend to begin near its ends. An intermediate type sits between the classic barred and unbarred forms, with a bar that is present but not dominant.
The data come from the Dark Energy Survey, a project that charted millions of galaxies. Surveys like this capture individual galaxies as a side benefit of their wider mapping work.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (17.27 x 17.76 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 276,000 × 284,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The image combines visible-light exposures from the Dark Energy Camera on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope, taken through g, r and i filters. The source does not say which display color was assigned to each filter.
